As it's time to make another post again, I thought I'd talk about something I think is important.

As the name suggests, this subverse would naturally be against angry mobs. Now, /v/ProtectVoat has just appeared, and I believe that in time it's going to be an angry mob, or at least an inquisition. So I thought since I have to make a post I'd talk about what I think about that.

I think that it's a bad idea. Firstly the name alone. That name divides people up. Protect Voat. It's a good mission statement if you like to keep it simple, but what does it actually mean? To me, it just sets people who use it up as the "good" guys, and the people they're after as the "bad" guys. The ones who are "against Voat." Already. they've been going after users and coming up with conspiracy theories. Already, they've resorted to name calling and inventing cabals, though that last part is really more like @Frankenmine.

If you give your subverse a name that makes you the "good guys" and people who are against it the "bad guys" you're going to cause trouble. That's what I think. Or maybe I'm reading too much into it and you just think you're doing the right thing. Most people do. But when you define anyone who doesn't agree with you as "The Enemy" you're asking for trouble. Even more so when you keep adding them to list of individuals in your fictional cabal just because they defended themselves or others.

Secondly, how can you criticise others when you are literally the ones forming a cabal? You've been collecting information on users to try and build a narrative wherein they're part of an SJW conspiracy to take over Voat, starting with /v/AskVoat. You're collecting information on users that you want to use to attack them later, for their beliefs or actions that you've twisted to mean something they don't, and you want to have a go at someone else for having a supposed cabal that takes place in a chat anyone can access?

In the end, I think it's just harmful to Voat. How can you claim to protect when, instead of uniting everyone, you're dividing the community into SJWs and Non-SJWs? How can you say that when you're proclaiming guilt before people have actually done anything, when some of your most active users have been very enthusiastic in inciting an angry mob against anyone deemed "SJW"?

In my opinion, /v/ProtectVoat will come to no good end. I think it supports an Us VS Them mentality that is unhealthy for Voat. It's a website designed for discussion. It relies on people to have interesting things to say, or interesting things said to them, or people get bored and they stop coming. If you drive out people for being "wrong", for being "too SJW", will you stop there? Or will there be some other threat you have to "protect" Voat from? Discussion websites work best when you have user diversity. You get more points of view that can be discussed. If you drive out people who don't fall in line, and I think you will, you'll kill what's good about Voat. A website designed to let everyone have their say is worthless if everyone is saying the same thing. I don't think ProtectVoat will come to a good end.
Feel free to discuss it. This is just my opinion, and a discussion could be good.
